findings.claim: "guard `MODIFIED=0 REMOVED=0` outside the write set" and "the guard still frames the write" — i.e. an independent, two-sided proof that the danger-full-access EXECUTE lane wrote only its declared file.
findings.why_it_fails: `diff workers/codex_lane/guard_before.txt workers/codex_lane/guard_after.txt` is EMPTY: the two files are byte-identical 106-line sha256 lists. `grep -c codex_writer guard_after.txt` = 0 — the artefact the guard is said to frame (`workers/codex_writer/EXECUTE_WRITER_RECEIPT.md`) is in neither snapshot. A fixed list of pre-existing paths hashed twice cannot observe an ADDITION, which is the only kind of effect a writer can produce and is exactly the shape of the one real escape (`HG-KSEOS/workers/codex_lane/EXEC_DISPATCH_RECEIPT.md`, a created file). So the control is structurally blind to its own failure mode, and 'MODIFIED=0 REMOVED=0' is a tautology: no file could ever be reported as added. This is load-bearing: the TT states 'The guard is what makes full access acceptable.'
findings.evidence_needed: A two-sided whole-tree digest (every path + sha256, both sides, new and deleted paths listed), or the guard re-run as `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` plus a full `find -newer` inventory across every governed repo, at both ends of the run. Re-state §8's bounded-write claim from that artefact, not from guard_before/after.

findings.claim: "`-s read-only` (which on this host refuses every process spawn)" therefore "`-s danger-full-access (mandatory on this host; read-only sandbox blocks all spawns)`", and `-s read-only` is listed under `never`.
findings.why_it_fails: The round's own §9 VERIFY dispatch receipt records `"sandbox": "read-only"` (receipts/dispatch/VERIFY_gpt61sol_judgement.json line 17) and its captured stdout shows two `command_execution` items with `exit_code: 0` — `Get-Content ... r152/verify2.md` and a pwsh `Get-Content workers/codex_lane/EXEC_DISPATCH_RECEIPT.md` that returned `LINES=4`. Read-only demonstrably spawns processes on this host. The §7 receipt the retraction is built on says the opposite of the retraction's mechanism: `blocked_by: "windows_sandbox_process_spawn_policy (reproduced identically under -s read-only AND -s workspace-write)"` — so the mode was never the variable; `--ignore-user-config` was. The retraction's cause analysis is therefore wrong, and the standing rule it produced ('full access is mandatory, never read-only') relaxes the sandbox for every future lane on a falsified premise — a premise that had just been used to justify a write into a governed repo.
findings.evidence_needed: Correct the TT and §8: state the measured variable (CODEX_HOME / `--ignore-user-config`) and drop the false 'read-only blocks all spawns' rule. Prove the corrected recipe under `-s read-only` (one gate run, exit 0, shell spawn observed), and re-issue the EXECUTE lane on read-only unless a write permit explicitly requires otherwise.

findings.claim: "All three stipulated arms now run through the sanctioned HGK dispatcher ... against pool `config/lane-route-slots.candidate.json` rev 20, with `--force-rank` + `--require-arm`" — presented as complaint-free, with VERIFY_SECURITY on `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` as PASS.
findings.why_it_fails: §3 (same document, same commit) says the opposite: the VERIFY lane at revision 32 binds `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, invoking gpt-6.1-sol 'would be a silent lane rebinding, which is forbidden without an owner-ordered registry change', recorded as TT-R15.2-VERIFY-LANE-SOD006-C6 OPEN_OWNER_ORDERED. §9 then performs exactly that selection and leaves the TT untouched (register regenerated at 21:31, after §9, still says OPEN_OWNER_ORDERED). The pool used also refutes the framing: its header is `"status": "CANDIDATE"` and `"claim_ceiling": "CANDIDATE_ONLY. Not promoted, not active."`, and its own `selection_note` records an owner order of 2026-10-21 that names gpt-6.1-sol as the checker model while rank 1 is still deepseek — so the run selected fallback1. Either the TT is stale (owner already ordered the checker model) or the run took an owner's call; the round states both and resolves neither. A candidate-plane fallback presented under the word 'sanctioned' is a claim the receipt does not carry.
findings.evidence_needed: One of: (a) the owner order (2026-10-21) quoted as the authority for gpt-6.1-sol on VERIFY, with the TT withdrawn and the pool promoted; or (b) a native config WorkOrder / registry-change receipt. Plus: §3 and §9 reconciled in one text, and the pool's CANDIDATE_ONLY ceiling restated in §9.

findings.target: STATUS_R15_2.md §9 preamble and 'Incident this produced' paragraph; LANE_DISPATCH_RECEIPTS.md line 4; receipts/dispatch/PLAN_gpt61sol.json
findings.claim: "`--cwd` pinned to this round directory" for every arm; "The **first** EXECUTE dispatch omitted `--cwd`, so the writer ran with cwd = HG-KSEOS".
findings.why_it_fails: The PLAN receipt that §9's own table cites (`receipts/dispatch/PLAN_gpt61sol.json`) records `"cwd": "C:\\Projects\\Agent_Workspace\\HG-KSEOS"` — the PLAN arm also ran inside the governed repo, and the incident paragraph counts only the EXECUTE dispatch as having escaped the pin. `grep -n -- '--cwd' scripts/hgk-lane-dispatch.py` confirms the default is documented as 'the repo root', so an omitted flag lands in HG-KSEOS silently, exactly as with EXECUTE. The same receipt also records `"role": "writer"` for the PLAN lane (EXECUTE is 'writer', VERIFY is 'checker'), so lane→role binding is not what the table implies. The undercount matters: the containment narrative is scoped to one dispatch, while at least two ran unpinned.
findings.evidence_needed: Correct §9 and the incident paragraph to state which dispatches ran with the default cwd, why PLAN was allowed to run in HG-KSEOS, and the role-binding defect. Add the dispatcher change (mandatory `--cwd`, refuse when absent) or a per-invocation receipt field proving the pin.

findings.target: TT_R15_2_REGISTER.json claim_ceiling + decision fields (NOFIT_ACCEPTED, RESOLVED_BY_REUSE_OF_PROVEN_LANE, CONTAINED_AND_DISCLOSED)
findings.claim: "claim_ceiling": "LOCAL_READ_ONLY_ADJUDICATION; no TT here is closed by an agent".
findings.why_it_fails: Three of the 13 items are closed by the agent that produced them: TT-R15.2-GSTACK-NOFIT `decision: NOFIT_ACCEPTED` on behalf of the Method Owner; TT-R15.2-CODEX-CLI-UNUSABLE `decision: RESOLVED_BY_REUSE_OF_PROVEN_LANE`, `owner: "none — closed by measurement"`; TT-R15.2-HGK-EXECUTE-CWD-ESCAPE `decision: CONTAINED_AND_DISCLOSED` with the round itself named as co-owner for a CRITICAL unauthorised write into a governed repo. The ceiling sentence is therefore false on its own file. The type discipline is also broken: `severity` holds `RESOLVED_MEASURED` and `CRITICAL_CONTAINED`, which are dispositions, not severities, so a machine consumer sorting by severity cannot rank this register. (`counts.hard_blocker` also read 0 at 21:2x and 3 at 21:31 — see F14.)
findings.evidence_needed: Restrict `decision` to OPEN | HOST_PENDING | NO_ACTION and re-issue each closure as an owner-signed disposition (Method Owner NoFit, HGK Native Owner containment, measurement closure). Put the disposition in a separate typed field, keep `severity` to CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|BLOCKER|INFO, and make claim_ceiling true for the file it heads.

findings.target: STATUS_R15_2.md §9 'Incident this produced, disclosed in full'; TT-R15.2-HGK-EXECUTE-CWD-ESCAPE (severity CRITICAL_CONTAINED)
findings.claim: "It was contained: bytes and tree captured (`receipts/incidents/`), the untracked `workers/` directory removed, and `git -C HG-KSEOS status --porcelain` verified empty with HEAD unchanged at `1760fb4`."
findings.why_it_fails: Two scoping defects. (1) The file labelled `..._before.txt` is timestamped `2026-10-22T13:26:43Z` while the dispatch it frames started at ~13:20:56 and timed out at 300.04s — it is a post-hoc inventory, not a pre-state, so it cannot exclude an earlier create-then-delete inside the same full-access window. (2) Containment is proven only for HG-KSEOS *tracked* files (I re-verified at review time: `git status --porcelain` empty, HEAD 1760fb443ab2…) and for the single write visible in the captured stream (1 write command among 113 `command_execution` items). Nothing covers writes to the other governed repos on this host or deletions of pre-existing untracked paths — and the receipt itself records `"side_effect_note": "danger-full-access has NO sandbox root: any absolute path is writable"` with `"subject_mutation": {"state": "not_guarded"}`. The class is also not contained: every later §9 run still used danger-full-access with an optional --cwd. A CRITICAL governed-repo write dispositioned 'CONTAINED' by the party that caused it, on evidence that proves less than the word implies, is not an admissible disposition.
findings.evidence_needed: An independent containment attestation: pre-run and post-run whole-tree digests of every governed repo (SBL, Fabric, HG-KSEOS, PIPD, SWOF) with timestamped pre-images, plus the dispatcher fix that makes --cwd mandatory and refuses otherwise. Until then the disposition must read 'CONTAINED_IN_ONE_REPO, CLASS_OPEN'.

findings.target: STATUS_R15_2.md §9 table and closing sentence; LANE_DISPATCH_RECEIPTS.md 'verify judgement'
findings.claim: "The VERIFY arm then judged the EXECUTE arm's artefact" with `"overclaims": [], "verdict": "PASS"`, and the table's `ok` column rendered as **PASS** for all three lanes.
findings.why_it_fails: The check is circular by construction. The VERIFY brief, captured verbatim in its own stdout (`receipts/dispatch/VERIFY_gpt61sol_judgement.json.logs/attempt-7260-...-stdout.txt`), contains the expected answer pre-filled: `{"nonce":"VERIFY-NONCE-3D90F2B6","receipt_present":true,...,"verdict":"PASS"|"FAIL"}`. The artefact it judges is a 4-line file whose `model:` line was dictated verbatim by the writer's brief (`workers/codex_lane/log_writer.log`, the Set-Content heredoc). So 'the model line matches what the writer declared' compares the orchestrator's prompt to itself; the checker verified file existence and line count (4) and nothing about model identity or scope. Meanwhile the dispatcher's own `claim_ceiling` — in every receipt — says 'a pass here proves the Codex-CLI lane served this turn through the relay with a matching usage receipt; it is not an acceptance of any subject', yet §9 prints PASS in the ok column with no per-row ceiling and closes with 'the role→model binding the user mandated is now demonstrated'. The same table's PLAN row is an 847-char three-key JSON outline (PLAN nonce + first_executable/blocked_on_native_permit), not the Commander-SP PLAN that §2 correctly keeps at NOT_RUN (C03/W03).
findings.evidence_needed: Re-run the checker with a prompt that does not contain the expected values, against an artefact whose model line is derived from the run's usage rows rather than typed by the brief. Label each row with the receipt's own claim_ceiling ('transport only'), and add an explicit line under the table: C03/W03/W04 remain NOT_RUN; these PASS values are lane-dispatch ok, not role execution.

findings.claim: "18 cards created and blocked" / `"state": "all blocked with reason NO_NATIVE_WORKORDER_PERMIT"`.
findings.why_it_fails: Half true. Read-only query of the live board DB (`.../hermes/kanban/boards/sbl-r15-2-20261022/kanban.db`) returns 18 tasks, `Counter({'blocked': 18})` — the state is real. The reason is not: `block_kind`, `last_failure_error` and `result` are NULL on all 18 rows, so `NO_NATIVE_WORKORDER_PERMIT` exists only in the prose. The cited receipt `receipts/kanban_cards.txt` shows creation only (18 `Wnn ... -> t_xxxx` lines, zero occurrences of 'blocked'), and `receipts/kanban_boards.txt` does not even list the new board.
findings.evidence_needed: Write the blocked reason into the board (or capture `hermes kanban show <id>` per card) and cite that capture instead. A machine-generated board dump with status + reason per card.

findings.claim: "`independent_check.json` ... 28/28 manifest files byte- and sha256-match, 0 mismatches, CONTRACT.json valid" offered as this round's self-check.
findings.why_it_fails: The check is stale. `independent_check.json` declares `file_count_declared: 28, file_count_actual: 28`; `ROUND_MANIFEST.json` now declares `"file_count": 154`. The 28-file check ran against an older manifest and says nothing about the 126 files added since — including every `receipts/dispatch/*` and `workers/codex_lane/*` artefact that §8/§9 rest on. Cited without a manifest digest, it reads as a current integrity result.
findings.evidence_needed: Re-run against the current manifest and record the manifest's own sha256 + file_count inside the check. The manifest already excludes itself; state that exclusion next to the result.

findings.claim: "raw logs ... the guard still frames the write"; recipe offered as reproducible ('Re-running requires re-copying the sealed home first' is presented as sufficient).
findings.why_it_fails: `receipt_missing: ["workers/codex_lane/home"]`, and the layered profiles `exe.config.toml`/`ver.config.toml` are explicitly not in the branch — so the exact invocation that produced the gate runs cannot be re-executed from the evidence. Worse, three different CODEX_HOME values describe the same recipe: dispatch receipts say `C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\HG-KSEOS\codex-hermes`, the gate log prints `...\round-20261022-r15_2\workers\codex_lane\home`, and RELOCATION_NOTE says `%TEMP%\r152\codex_home_isolated`. 'Byte-reproducible as recorded' is not supported while the config that defines the run is absent and the home is ambiguous.
findings.evidence_needed: One canonical CODEX_HOME per run, recorded in the receipt; profiles committed with credentials stripped, or a deterministic regeneration step; and a re-run of one gate from the committed recipe proving the path.

findings.target: STATUS_R15_2.md §9 'Two refusals proved the gate is real'
findings.claim: `--require-arm gpt-6.1-sol` alone returns `ERR_LANE_REQUIRED_ARM_ABSENT`, and 'a run with no nonce in an agent message cannot pass even at exit 0'.
findings.why_it_fails: No receipt exists for either refusal: `grep -rl ERR_LANE_REQUIRED_ARM_ABSENT` returns nothing under the round, and `receipts/dispatch/` contains only the three successful resolutions plus the timed-out EXECUTE. findings.claim: STATUS §1 rows 3-6: the four official CAPC commands 'exit 0' with `contract_sha256 = 414005c1…`.
findings.why_it_fails: On substance this one SURVIVES: I re-ran `python scripts/prompt_contract_compiler.py {lint,activation,acceptance} CONTRACT.json` against the frozen bundle and got exit 0 + `PROMPT_COMPILE_PASS` + error_count 0 each time, and `sha256sum CONTRACT.json` matches 414005c1… exactly. The defect is only evidential hygiene: the receipts are hand-assembled `# command:` comment headers over a JSON body with **no exit code field**, so the 'exit 0' in the table is not carried by the artefact it cites.
findings.evidence_needed: Capture raw stdout+stderr and the exit code per command (or note that the exit code was re-measured at review). Low priority; the claim is true.

findings.claim: `"commit": "from R14_LEDGER_READBACK.json.source_commit"` and 'For each of the 7 suspect items: locate the artefact ... or downgrade the item'.
findings.why_it_fails: The item that exists to adjudicate ledger divergence does not name the commit it read — an unsubstituted template string, while R14_LEDGER_READBACK.json holds the real value `e6623ba1e9a4a477d07048cd3a5a906f33d6029d`. The 7 `suspect_items` also mix two populations: `done_items_with_gaps` is 5 (TS09, TS14, TS18, TS21, TS24) while TS10 and TS11 come from `in_branch_missing_paths` and are already PARTIAL/BLOCKED, so 'downgrade the item' does not apply to them. The counts themselves check out (17/9/1/4 = 31; 12/17 DONE fully evidenced; 20/10/1 classification), so the defect is in the register, not the readback.
findings.evidence_needed: Substitute the commit sha and split the suspect list into 'DONE with gaps (5)' and 'in-branch missing paths (2)', with the action per group.

findings.claim: The round is a closed artefact (STATUS/TT/MANIFEST at 21:28) offered for a single verdict.
findings.why_it_fails: The subject moved during this review. At 21:29 TT_R15_2_REGISTER.json was 20,875 bytes with `"hard_blocker": 0`; at 21:31:06 it was 20,945 bytes with `"hard_blocker": 3` and a new `receipt_missing` key on TT-R15.2-CODEX-CLI-UNUSABLE; ROUND_MANIFEST.json went 26,906 → 27,554 bytes and `file_count` 28-era → 154 at 21:32:15. STATUS_R15_2.md did not change (21:28:37). A verdict bound to a digest that changes under the reviewer cannot be replayed — and in this case the change silently repaired a real defect (hard_blocker 0 → 3), which is exactly the kind of edit a review is supposed to catch rather than receive.
findings.evidence_needed: Freeze the round directory (or a manifest digest of it) before review, and re-issue the corrected TT as a new revision with its own sha and a change note. Do not edit the register while a verdict is being formed.

Correct the Codex cause analysis: prove the corrected CODEX_HOME recipe under `-s read-only` with an observed spawn, drop the false 'read-only blocks all spawns' rule, and stop mandating danger-full-access as a host requirement.

Reconcile §3 with §9 and close TT-R15.2-VERIFY-LANE-SOD006-C6 one way or the other: quote the owner order that authorises gpt-6.1-sol on VERIFY (and promote the pool off CANDIDATE), or withdraw the force-rank run and re-dispatch on the assigned arm.
State, per dispatch, whether --cwd was pinned; disclose that the PLAN arm also ran with cwd = HG-KSEOS; make --cwd mandatory in hgk-lane-dispatch.py.

Re-run the checker with a non-leading prompt against an artefact whose model line comes from the run's usage rows; label every lane row 'transport only' and add an explicit C03/W03/W04 NOT_RUN line under the §9 table.
Make claim_ceiling true for the TT register: no decision may be NOFIT_ACCEPTED / RESOLVED_* / CONTAINED_* unless an owner signed it; keep severity to severity values only.
Give the CWD-escape incident an independent containment attestation over all governed repos plus a timestamped pre-image, or downgrade it to CONTAINED_IN_ONE_REPO, CLASS_OPEN.
Write the Kanban blocked reason into the board (or capture `kanban show` per card), re-run the manifest self-check against the current 154-file manifest, and freeze the round before the next verdict.
